about: The nightly integrity watch on a database the clean start has just reset (design final.first_night_integrity): the statuses each check may have on the reset day (night1, right after COMMIT) and on the next Oman morning (night2, 02:30 UTC). A check missing here, or a status not listed, is a mismatch. rehearse-watch.ts asserts it; tests/integration/clean-start.test.ts runs it.

withForeignSeals.about: When PLAN found objects under seals/ that are not production's chain (another environment's chain folder, a non-seal object), the first run reports each once, as new and critical, and the next as information. Accepted ONLY when every open finding is one of those pre-listed keys.

night2NotAssertedBeforeUtcHour.about: Night 2 is simulated at 02:30 UTC of the Oman day after night 1's, and reads the job runs of night 1's Oman day. The windowed jobs of that day run 03:00-15:00 UTC on its calendar date, so a copy taken before 15:00 UTC on that date cannot hold them all: their gaps would be real absences in the copy, not on production. The check is then reported, not asserted. That is every rehearsal before 15:00 UTC, and every one after midnight in Oman (20:00 UTC), whose Oman day has only begun (rehearse-watch.ts jobDayCompleteAt).

sealWrittenResult.about: The status of seal-written cannot tell a seal that was written from one that was not: a second run on the same Oman day answers 'already' and is still a pass. Night 1 must write the new chain's first seal (genesis) and night 2 the first seal chained to it (sealed). Anything else is a mismatch.
